chapter: Touring shows and the bands he heard
title: His father's embouchure lesson
summary: His father tried to teach him double embouchure; he declined and went his own way.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So my father came, and we talked... And he made an attempt at giving me some lessons. He wanted me to play what they called double embrochure at the time, because... In other words, the way I play is like single embrochure, where you put your top teeth on the mouthpiece and your lip over your bottom teeth. But he put his top lip over the top teeth and his bottom lip over the bottom teeth. And they claimed that that way you could play a brass and reed instrument, and it wouldn't split the tone, some kind of way... They talk about splitting the tone if you didn't play double embrochure. And that hurt, and I didn't want to deal with that. So I cut my Dad a little, and I said, 'No, I'll just go my own way.' [LAUGHS] I wasn't going to go through that; you know, try to play that way.
So anyway, we all went down to catch the Silas Green Show every time it came to town.
